Your answer
The 2010 Jeep Patriot welcomes travel enthusiasts with a loaded cache of standard equipment,
®
including Electronic Stability Control (ESC)(1) with Electronic Roll Mitigation (ERM), a four-wheel
antilock brake system (ABS), and traction control.
Standard fog lamps, 17-inch cast aluminum wheels and silver body-side molding help Patriot Limited
make an impressive appearance both on the trail and off. Limiteds equipped with an automatic
transmission also include a new and standard Tip Start that gets your engine going with a simple flick
of the wrist. The new available heated power side mirrors are a functional safety and security feature.
A 6-way power driver seat is new and standard on Limited.
Authentic Jeep brand good looks give Patriot Sport a naturally attractive profile, with a body-color
seven-slot grille, door handles, and liftgate applique. Sport gives you two window choices: the chic,
unique option of manual roll-ups or available power windows with driver’s one-touch down. Either
way you’re looking good.
(1)N o system, no matter how sophisticated, can repeal the laws of physics or overcome careless driving actions. Performance is limited
by available traction, which snow, ice and other conditions can affect. When the ESC warning lamp in the speedometer flashes,
the driver needs to use less throttle and adapt speed and driving behavior to prevailing road conditions. Always drive carefully,
consistent with conditions. Always wear your seat belt.
rearrange your world.
Patriot’s configurable interior lets you arrange things to your liking. The standard 60/40 fold-flat rear seats offer an
available recline feature for up to 12 degrees of added rear seat relaxation. When you answer the call of the wild,
be sure to properly secure all cargo.
